findings.summary: slot() falls back to an '(unknown)' week for ANY unparseable date, including costed shifts. labourIsoWeek_ throws on a bad date, so the two paths disagree: a costed shift with a missing/malformed date is silently bucketed with weekStart '' instead of failing loudly, and its money lands in an '(unknown)' row.
findings.suggestion: Only apply the '(unknown)' fallback for exceptions (line 507). For costed shifts, call labourIsoWeek_(s.date) directly and let it throw, consistent with the department-disagreement rule. Add a test: a costed shift with date '' THROWS.

findings.summary: labourIsoWeek_ accepts calendar-impossible dates such as '2026-02-30' and silently normalises them to 2026-03-02 via Date.UTC overflow; the regex only checks shape.
findings.suggestion: Round-trip check after Date.UTC (getUTCMonth()/getUTCDate() must equal the input parts) and throw on mismatch, matching the bad-format throw.

findings.summary: Exception-only rows always have department '' because exception objects carry no department, so step 4 cannot tell which department an exception-only location belongs to. Not wrong per the brief, but it is an unstated gap in the row shape.
findings.suggestion: Document in the labourGroup_ header comment that exception-only rows have department ''. Or let step 4 look the department up from the location config.
